title: Lead workflow engine: legality matrix, all lead operations, status history, pricing approvals, follow-ups, availableOperations
objective: Port the lead workflow: a pure legality-matrix module (operation x status by reporting category + canonical key), the full lead operation set executed via POST /leads/{id}/operations/{op} with append-only status history (actor/inputs), pricing-approval sub-state with optional high-value gate, follow-up logging, the single Assign/Reassign dialog contract over fixed slots, and server-computed availableOperations (P-07).
scope: Pure module domains/leads/workflow/legality.ts: legal operations per status evaluated by reporting category + canonical key; unit-tested against the full ported matrix

Operations: assign (slots; accountable owner = rm), start-information-gathering, send-to-underwriting, start-pricing, request-pricing-approval, approve-pricing, reject-pricing, log-follow-up, start-negotiation, mark-lost (structured reason + comment-when-Other + open-quote cascade), withdraw, reopen (to last open status)
Append-only lead_status_history with actor + jsonb inputs per operation; audit rows per P-13
Pricing approval as a Pricing sub-state with the tenant-toggled high-value send gate (business rule)
follow_ups records via log-follow-up (next-follow-up requirements enforced where the matrix requires)
availableOperations computed server-side and returned on lead detail per contract; 409 with legal-operation hint on illegal transitions
Only jobs make automatic status changes (expiry paths live in T-032)
out_of_scope: Quote operations (T-026 — including won->lead Closed Won cascade from the quote side)
Alert re-evaluation enqueue hook (T-034 wires it into these executors)
implementation_details: Port LeadOperationExecutor semantics: each operation validates legality (matrix), validates inputs (zod per-operation schemas — assignee eligibility, lost reason from reference list active values, follow-up dates future while open, etc.), mutates state, appends history, writes audit, stamps last_activity_at — all in one transaction.
Reopen: returns to the last open status from history (port exact resolution rule).
Mark-lost cascade: open quotes of the lead transition per reference cascade rules with their own history entries.
Assign/Reassign: single dialog contract — slot-based payload (rm/underwriter), validates role-holders per T-020 slots.
availableOperations: same legality module + per-user permission filtering as the reference (illegal ops hidden in UI, but server also rejects).
Executor emits an in-process domain event/callback seam so T-034 can enqueue targeted alert re-evaluation without modifying operation logic.

unit: Full legality matrix: every operation x status combination matches the ported .NET matrix (table-driven); reporting-category + canonical-key evaluation; reopen target resolution
integration: Each operation: state change + history row (actor, inputs jsonb) + audit + last_activity_at, atomically; illegal op -> 409 with legal-operation hint
Pricing approval flow incl. high-value gate on/off via business rule; approve/reject transitions
Mark-lost with reason/comment rules + quote cascade; withdraw; reopen to last open status
availableOperations reflects status + permissions for different fixture users
e2e: Lead workflow specs (dialogs, operations) adapted in T-043

findings.summary: AC-049's high-value pricing gate does not exist on any LEAD operation in the reference - it is a QUOTE-send rule owned by T-026
findings.detail: AC-049 and this task's scope state that 'when the tenant's pricing-approval gate is enabled and the lead is high-value, send-path progress requires an approved pricing state (attempt without it -> 409)'. MEASURED: the only implementation of that rule in the reference is SendQuoteCommandHandler.cs:85-91 - it reads settings.RequirePricingApprovalForHighValue, settings.HighValueThreshold and the CURRENT QUOTE VERSION's QuotedPremium, and returns QuoteWorkflowErrors.PricingApprovalRequired ('PRICING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED', 422 - NOT 409). No lead operation consults RequirePricingApprovalForHighValue at all (grep over src/api: the only non-settings, non-dashboard reference is SendQuoteCommandHandler). There is no lead-side 'send path'. The gate is therefore NOT implementable in T-025 and belongs to T-026, which this task's own out_of_scope already assigns quote operations to. Two further contradictions with AC-049 for the record: the status is 422 not 409, and the threshold is compared against the QUOTE's premium, not the lead's estimated premium. IMPLEMENTED HERE: the pricing-approval SUB-STATE machine in full (request/approve/reject, none->pending->approved|rejected, approver eligibility, approver and reason recorded, audited, and the re-request-after-rejection rework loop) - everything in AC-049 except the send gate. FLAGGED rather than filled: a lead-side high-value gate would invent behaviour the reference does not have. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-19T17:10:00-04:00): VERIFIED FIRST-HAND against the reference: the only high-value pricing gate is SendQuoteCommandHandler.cs:85-91 - QUOTE-side, inside the quote Send operation, returns 422 PRICING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED (QuoteWorkflowErrors.cs:26-29, whose own doc comment says '422, nothing persists'), and compares the CURRENT QUOTE VERSION's QuotedPremium against the threshold. A repo-wide grep confirms no lead operation consults RequirePricingApprovalForHighValue. AC-049's send-gate clause is a false premise on the lead side: wrong entity, wrong status code, wrong premium field, and no lead-side send path exists. ESCALATED TO THE HUMAN, left open. RECOMMENDATION: amend AC-049 to the measured contract - keep the pricing sub-state clauses (implemented and verified here) in T-025's scope, and re-scope the gate clause to T-026 as 'quote Send with the tenant gate enabled and the current version's premium above threshold requires pricing_approval_state=approved; attempt without it -> 422 PRICING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, nothing persists', with V-063's second bullet re-pointed at the quote-send path. This is the same class the human just ruled on for T-024-F4, in favour of amending to the measured contract.

findings.summary: 409 legal-operation hint is named `availableOperations`, not the reference's `legalOperations`
findings.detail: LeadWorkflowErrors.IllegalTransition puts the hint in an extension called `legalOperations`. T-009 had already shipped lib/errors/index.ts and lib/errors/problem.ts with the extension named `availableOperations`, pinned by tests/unit/problem.test.ts and tests/integration/http.skeleton.test.ts. This port reuses T-009's IllegalOperationError rather than renaming a shipped, pinned contract in another task's files. Verified no consumer is affected: grep over src/ui finds zero occurrences of `legalOperations`; the SPA reads `availableOperations` off the LEAD DTO and never parses the 409 body's hint. Recorded, not silently chosen - if byte-for-byte parity with the reference is wanted, it is a one-line change in lib/errors/problem.ts plus its two pins, and that is a T-009 decision. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-19T17:10:00-04:00): ACCEPTED. Verified: the reference names the hint legalOperations (LeadWorkflowErrors.cs:16); T-009's shipped problem writer names it availableOperations, pinned by two suites; the only 'legalOperations' hit under src/ui is the substring inside a test NAME (LeadDetailPage.test.tsx:177 'IllegalOperationsNotInAvailableOperations') - the SPA never parses the 409 hint field. No shipped consumer is affected, and renaming a pinned T-009 contract from inside T-025 would be worse than the divergence. Should be transcribed into AC-095's documented-deviation ledger when T-044 evaluates contract parity.

findings.summary: The executor's own LEAD_OPERATION_FORBIDDEN is unreachable over HTTP; the route guard answers first with no domain code
findings.detail: MEASURED: requirePermission (lib/auth/require-permission.ts:141) throws a bare ForbiddenError with NO `code` extension. Because the route guard and the executor consult the SAME per-operation permission map, an HTTP caller lacking the permission is always rejected by the guard, so the executor's LEAD_OPERATION_FORBIDDEN never appears on the wire. That matches the reference's double-gating (LeadWorkflowEndpoints.cs:27-28 calls it 'defense in depth') and is correct - the executor's check exists for NON-HTTP callers (the T-032 expiry job, queue handlers, cascades) that pass no route guard. Covered accordingly: the HTTP test asserts the guard's 403 and that the body leaks nothing about the lead, and a separate test calls withdrawLead() directly with a real EffectiveAccess built over an empty permission set to reach the executor's own 403 and prove nothing was written. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-19T17:10:00-04:00): RULED SOUND, not a hidden gap. Verified requirePermission throws a bare ForbiddenError with no code (require-permission.ts:141) and shares the executor's per-operation permission map (routes.ts literal permissions match LEAD_OPERATION_PERMISSIONS and the reference's LeadOperationPermissions.cs exactly), so the executor's LEAD_OPERATION_FORBIDDEN is genuinely unreachable over HTTP. The suite asserts the true wire contract (guard 403, no lead disclosure) AND reaches the executor's own check by calling withdrawLead() directly with an access object that denies everything, proving 403 + no writes. Strengthening the HTTP test to expect the domain code would have been asserting a fiction. Evaluator-side correction applied: the test comment at lead-workflow.test.ts:1393 claimed the access object was 'not a hand-rolled stub' when it is one; reworded to describe reality (behaviour unchanged, suites re-run green).

findings.summary: Quote-side statuses (Quote Sent, Negotiation) are constructed by direct SQL in the test fixture, because T-026 does not exist yet
findings.detail: start-negotiation is legal only from canonical `quote_sent`, and the log-follow-up 'future next date required past Quote Sent' rule only applies to reporting category `quoted`. Neither status is reachable by any LEAD operation - they are entered from the quote side (T-026). Rather than declaring those rules untestable, the discriminating state is constructed directly by SQL (forceStatus(), which also appends a truthful history row so reopen's history walk has something real to find). This converts three otherwise unfalsifiable rules into covered ones: start-negotiation, the log-follow-up quoted-category gate, and lostBeforeQuote=false. Once T-026 lands, forceStatus() should be replaced by a real quote-send call. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-19T17:10:00-04:00): ACCEPTED as the only honest way to test quote-side-entered statuses before T-026 exists; forceStatus() appends a truthful history row so reopen's walk sees real data. KEPT OPEN as a tracked follow-up: once T-026 lands, replace forceStatus() with a real quote-send call. T-026's evaluator should check this.

findings.summary: Alert re-evaluation seam is an optional post-commit callback for T-034 to wire
findings.detail: LeadOperationExecutor called IAlertReevaluationQueue.EnqueueLeadReevaluationAsync inside its transaction. Here it is LeadWorkflowDeps.onLeadChanged, an OPTIONAL callback invoked AFTER commit - enqueuing re-evaluation for a state that may still roll back is how duplicate and phantom alerts get created. Nothing wires it yet; T-034 supplies it without modifying any operation logic. EVALUATOR RULING (2026-07-19T17:10:00-04:00): Informational design record, no action for T-025. Moving the alert re-evaluation enqueue from inside the transaction to a post-commit callback is an improvement over the reference (no phantom/duplicate alerts from rolled-back state); T-034 wires it.
